name: FeetFinder
summary: The most established dedicated marketplace for foot content, operating since 2019 and now home to Instafeet's former buyers. Its large verified buyer base and discovery system surface new sellers from day one, so you don't need an existing following to make your first sale.

name: Footly
summary: A newer, mobile-first platform built around an algorithmic feed instead of a static profile grid. Discovery for new profiles is promising, but its buyer base is still growing, so it works best as a second platform once your main profile is earning.

name: Feetify
summary: A community-focused platform with monthly contests, comments and tips, plus a tiered commission that improves the more active you are. Fewer independent reviews exist, so confirm the payout terms before relying on it.

name: OnlyFans
summary: A huge subscription platform with no seller fee and a 20% cut, but no built-in discovery for foot content. Great if you already have a social following to bring with you; a weak starting point for complete beginners.

name: Fansly
summary: A direct OnlyFans competitor with a reported 10–20% commission and strong tools for social traffic. Like OnlyFans, internal discovery is minimal, so it still needs an audience you bring yourself.

name: Snifffr
summary: An adult-oriented marketplace covering foot content, worn items and custom videos. Listing is free, but commission terms aren't clearly published and its positioning won't suit sellers who want a neutral, commercial feel.

name: Fun With Feet
summary: A feet-focused storefront with a flat subscription and a 15% commission. Payments and verification are legitimate, but buyers don't find you on their own, so it suits creators who can drive their own traffic from social media.

name: FeetPics
summary: A commission-only platform with no monthly fee, which makes it a risk-free way to test what sells. Buyer activity is lower than on the big marketplaces, so first sales can take a while.

name: JustFor.Fans
bestFor: Free and paid tiers on one profile
summary: Lets you mix free previews and paid content on the same profile, which can lift conversions. Commission sits around 15–20% and natural discovery is limited, so treat its promo events as a bonus, not a plan.

name: DollarFeet
summary: You apply, submit content to their specs and the platform handles buyers and pricing. There's no storefront to run, but you give up pricing control and the income ceiling is lower than a self-managed profile.

name: Foap
summary: A stock photo marketplace that pays 50% of each license. Clean, commercial foot, footwear and pedicure images can earn royalties again and again, but per-sale earnings are small and adult content isn't allowed.

name: DepositPhotos
summary: A standard stock agency paying 30–50% per download depending on your level. Brands buy foot imagery for shoe, pedicure and foot-care campaigns here, but income builds slowly over months.

name: Shutterstock
summary: One of the largest stock agencies in the world, paying roughly 15–40% per download by earnings tier. Its strict quality review makes it a poor fit for beginners, but a solid long-term option for skilled photographers.

name: Instafeet
summary: Once a well-known standalone marketplace, Instafeet was acquired by and folded into FeetFinder. If an article still points you to Instafeet as a separate site, it hasn't been updated; its audience is now reached through FeetFinder.
